findings.title: Use OR for team admin or owner authorization
findings.body: The team authorization requires both isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner to succeed. Admin and owner are distinct membership roles, so a team administrator or owner who is not also the booking organizer or an attendee is denied permission to add guests. Combine these checks with OR to implement the intended admin-or-owner permission.

findings.title: Update the calendar using the booking organizer's credentials
findings.body: The handler permits attendees and team administrators to add guests, but constructs EventManager with the requesting user's credentials rather than the booking organizer's. When an attendee adds a guest, the calendar reference belongs to the organizer and cannot be updated using the attendee's calendar credentials. This leaves the persisted attendee list out of sync with the organizer's calendar (or fails after the database insert). Use the booking owner's credentials for the calendar update.

findings.title: Deduplicate incoming guests on the server
findings.body: uniqueGuests only filters against existing booking attendees; it does not remove duplicates within the incoming guests array, and the server schema accepts duplicate addresses. A direct mutation with the same email twice therefore passes both entries to createMany, creating duplicate attendees or failing on a database uniqueness constraint. The dialog's client-side refinement does not protect this endpoint; validate or deduplicate the request on the server.

findings.title: Normalize guest addresses before checking the blacklist
findings.body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased, but incoming guest addresses are compared without lowercasing. A blacklisted address submitted with uppercase characters passes this filter and receives an invitation. Normalize incoming addresses before blacklist comparison and persistence.

findings.title: Honor disabled standard email settings for guest additions
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally emails the organizer and every attendee, unlike the other booking notification functions which respect eventTypeDisableHostEmail and eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail. Consequently, adding guests sends standard emails even for event types configured to disable them, including existing attendees who should receive no standard notifications. Pass the event type metadata through the handler and apply the same suppression checks here.
